title: Software Engineer, Traffic Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and the API. Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.

Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering. We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI’s products and services across clouds and regions. The team’s work spans L3, L4, and L7—from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.

You’ll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works. Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.

This role combines software engineering with production ownership. You’ll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.

 - Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.

 - Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.

 - Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.

 - Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.

 - Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.

 - Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.

 - Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience building production infrastructure or distributed systems, including substantial work on networking or traffic infrastructure.

 - Have depth in one or more areas such as cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, proxies and gateways, service meshes, load balancing, or global traffic routing.

 - Understand networking fundamentals and can reason about how IP routing, TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT, TLS, and HTTP/gRPC affect connectivity and performance.

 - Have hands-on experience building or operating systems such as Envoy, NGINX, Istio, Cilium, or comparable networking infrastructure.

 - Write production software in Go, Rust, C++, Python, or a similar language, and use software and automation to solve operational problems.

 - Can investigate unfamiliar failures using evidence, test hypotheses, and follow problems through to a verified resolution.

 - Take ownership of design, implementation, rollout, and ongoing reliability, and communicate clearly across teams when a problem crosses ownership boundaries.

 - Care about making infrastructure secure and understandable for the engineers who depend on it.

We value deep expertise and the willingness to learn across boundaries. You do not need prior experience with every technology or networking layer listed above.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
description:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

 - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

 - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

 - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

 - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

 - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

 - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

 - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

 - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

 - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Motion Designer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications.

Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll help determine what a story needs visually, explore different approaches, and bring those ideas to life through thoughtful design and animation.

This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and the ability to find a compelling visual approach when the brief is still taking shape. You’ll contribute to how OpenAI’s research is expressed in motion, developing original work and reusable approaches that help the team build on what it learns.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to understand the ideas and identify how best to communicate them.

 - Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content.

 - Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story.

 - Take work from visual exploration, storyboards, and animatics through animation, compositing, and final delivery.

 - Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers, bringing a motion perspective into the creative process early.

 - Translate technical or abstract concepts into visual sequences that are accessible to a broad audience while preserving the meaning of the underlying work.

 - Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve.

 - Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners.

 - Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work.

 - A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution.

 - The ability to explore an open-ended brief, propose a clear creative direction, and refine it through collaboration.

 - Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows.

 - Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams.

The People team helps OpenAI attract, engage, and support the exceptional talent this work requires.

Employer Brand sits at the intersection of Research, Recruiting, Communications, Marketing, and Brand. Reporting to the Employer Brand Manager, you’ll help translate our employer brand strategy into stories and campaigns that help candidates understand our work, our people, and the opportunity to contribute to our mission.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with broad employer brand responsibilities and a particular focus on writing, content planning, digital, and social storytelling. You’ll develop content that reflects the experiences of our researchers and employees, adapt stories for different audiences and channels, and help deliver a consistent, credible candidate experience.

title: Trusted Access Specialist, Critical Harm Operations
description:
About the team

Trusted Access helps eligible customers access and use advanced AI capabilities with appropriate safeguards. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence.

We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior operator to own and improve the customer access workflow for an assigned Trusted Access program. You will connect application and eligibility review, approvals, appeals, provisioning coordination, and support so customers can reach a clear, reliable outcome.

Your primary focus will be improving how the program works. You’ll use complex customer cases to uncover recurring problems, then deliver product, automation, self-service, and support-process improvements. You’ll also own difficult eligibility and access escalations, helping customers and account teams understand what is blocking progress and driving the right partners toward resolution.

This role combines independent workflow ownership with hands-on operational judgment. Success means customers reach usable access with fewer avoidable delays, decisions remain accurate, and the workflow runs reliably through the people and systems you enable.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the operational workflow for an assigned Trusted Access program, from application through confirmed access and subsequent changes. Identify where customers get stuck and prioritize improvements by customer impact, risk, and effort.

 - Investigate complex eligibility, onboarding, and access cases. Reconcile approval, verification, account, workspace, and provisioning records; apply approved requirements within your authority and bring exceptions to the appropriate decision-maker.

 - Drive customer and account-team escalations through resolution. Establish the blocker, maintain clear ownership across handoffs, communicate realistic next steps, and confirm that the customer can use the intended capability.

 - Turn recurring case patterns into product and process changes with Product, Engineering, and customer-facing partners. Define the problem and requirements, help validate the fix, and measure whether it reduced repeat contacts or manual work.

 - Build guidance that makes reliable resolution repeatable: support playbooks, help-center content, training, and quality checks. Enable frontline and outsourced support teams to handle more cases accurately and independently.

 - Use data to distinguish fast ticket closure from better access outcomes. Diagnose delays, rework, and decision errors, and use the findings to refine your workflow and priorities.

 - Develop and validate AI-assisted workflows and automation with technical partners. Establish checks, human review, and fallback paths appropriate to the decisions involved.

 - Maintain clear documentation and qualified backup across programs. Share what you learn so improvements continue working when another specialist takes ownership.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have independently owned and improved customer support, onboarding, access, risk, or product-operations workflows in a complex service environment.

 - Can show durable improvements you delivered through product changes, self-service, automation, or partner enablement, with evidence of adoption and better customer outcomes.

 - Exercise sound judgment when records conflict, requirements are unclear, or customers need urgent help. You can separate what the evidence supports from what still needs an authorized decision.

 - Are comfortable investigating across customer, account, approval, and access systems, and can translate operational problems into clear requirements for technical partners.

 - Use operational data to identify root causes, prioritize work, and evaluate whether a change improved the service.

 - Communicate with clarity and empathy under pressure, and can explain a difficult access decision or unresolved blocker without making unsupported commitments.

 - Build trust across teams you do not manage and follow through from a proposed improvement to reliable day-to-day operation.

title: Land and Data Center Development
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Compute organization builds the infrastructure that powers frontier AI training and inference. This work brings together commercial, technical, strategy, and operations teams to secure and develop the sites and capacity needed for large-scale compute deployment.

We partner across real estate, power, engineering, legal, finance, and delivery to connect infrastructure needs with viable development opportunities and executable commercial agreements.

About the Role

We’re looking for a commercial real estate (CRE) development professional to help secure land and data-center capacity for OpenAI’s compute infrastructure. This is a combined role spanning land acquisition and development, data-center leasing, and real estate acquisitions. The ideal candidate is particularly strong in land and can also contribute across data-center transactions.

You’ll source and evaluate opportunities, structure and negotiate agreements, and coordinate commercial and technical diligence. Working with legal, finance, engineering, and development partners, you’ll connect transaction decisions with infrastructure requirements and carry opportunities through agreement execution and handoff.

Responsibilities

 - Lead sourcing, evaluation, and commercial execution of land acquisition opportunities for data-center development.

 - Support data-center leasing and real estate acquisitions, working across land and data-center transactions as priorities require.

 - Build relationships with landowners, brokers, developers, and data-center counterparties to source opportunities.

 - Structure and negotiate land acquisition, site-control, and data-center lease agreements with legal and business partners.

 - Coordinate diligence with legal, finance, engineering, and development partners, translating site constraints and readiness risks into commercial decisions.

 - Evaluate deal economics and present clear recommendations on costs, terms, tradeoffs, and next steps.

 - Manage the transaction pipeline, keep stakeholders aligned, and resolve issues that affect decisions and execution.

title: Incident Commander, Detection & Response - APAC
description:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective.

In this role, you will:

 - Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs.

 - Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

 - Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights.

 - Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions.

 - Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners.

 - Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes.

 - Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact.

 - Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs.

 - Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty.

 - Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options.

 - Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions.

 - Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling.

title: Fire Protection Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners.

The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations.

About the Role

We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses.

 - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases.

 - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems.

 - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems.

 - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks.

 - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction.

 - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems.

 - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities.

 - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards.

 - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements.

 - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems.

 - 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments.

 - Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes.

 - Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems.

 - Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results.

 - Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders.

 - Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous.

 - Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs.

 - Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis.

 - Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces.

 - Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites.

Join us on our mission and shape the future!



Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans - by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting text output, you will improve Large Language Model’s performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere’s tech.


Cohere seeks dynamic and dedicated Data Annotators with exceptional Modern Standard German Writing, Translation, and Data Manipulation skill.



Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada. We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 30 CAD/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 - Bring Your Own Device (laptop). Remote work within Canada. 12 months contract. Performance incentives included!



As a Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Label and Rank: Accurately label and rank machine learning data with advanced proficiency in German, ensuring data integrity and quality.

 - Audit and Correct: Scrutinize and rectify any inaccuracies in language data (may include text, image, JSON, TSV/CSV, Markdown), maintaining the highest standard of data accuracy.

 - Reading and Text-Based Tasks: Efficiently complete reading and text-based assignments, with high attention to detail.

 - Preference-Based Tasks: Evaluate and complete tasks, assessing which responses in German best conform to project guidelines.

 - Recommend Optimizations: Identify and suggest opportunities for improving data quality and model performance in German language tasks.

 - Provide Feedback: Collaborate and communicate effectively, providing feedback to cross-functional team members, particularly on German language-related matters.

 - Detail-Oriented Execution: Maintain meticulous attention to detail while performing repetitive and precise tasks, particularly when working with language data.



You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Language Proficiency: Native or near-native proficiency in German; excellent command over English.

 - Expert reading and writing skills - which you are ready to prove on our written test.

 - Basic familiarity with JSON/TSV/CSV/Markdown data manipulation.

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy - you’re the type to proofread all of your emails!

 - High tolerance for repetitive and monotonous work.

 - Ability to follow complex instructions, navigate ambiguity and work independently.

 - Superb sense of urgency and time management.

 - Curiosity about technology and a knack for tackling problems in creative ways.

 - A reliable laptop.



The Candidate Journey:
Initial Screening - Once you have submitted your application our Talent Team will review your resume and writing samples.
Virtual Annotation Test -  This assignment will test your written skill through various language-based tasks, such as a a writing sample, interacting with a chat bot, and more.
Video Screen - If selected to move forward, you will have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team!
Offer - Independent Contractor Agreement


As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and therefore compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human generated and model generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.



If some of the above doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

description:

Why this role?

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.


In this role, you will:

 - Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation.

 - Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale.

 - Work with researchers and training-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements

 - Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the measures of success
   

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.

 - Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other

 - Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.
   

It’s a bonus if you have:

 - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.

 - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training.

 - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving.

Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models, to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans, by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting model output, you will improve Large Language Models' performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere's technology. We are hiring Generalist professionals with broad backgrounds that span multiple consumer-facing or personal domains.

This is a judgment-driven role, not passive data entry. You will review, assess, and provide structured feedback across a broad and evolving range of tasks, evaluating, stress-testing, and improving our models on English-language data spanning multiple modalities (text, image, and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, and Markdown). This is a great opportunity for professionals with strong analytical skills to contribute to high-impact annotation projects.

Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada only. We seek candidates who can commit to 16 hours per week at a CAD $30/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 (Bring Your Own Device, laptop). This position is remote.

As an Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Evaluate and rank model outputs: Complete preference and comparison tasks, assessing which responses best conform to project guidelines for accuracy, helpfulness, tone, and safety, and writing clear justifications for your judgments.

 - Stress-test and break models: Probe models adversarially to surface failure modes, unsafe behavior, and capability gaps, and document reproducible cases that engineering and research teams can act on.

 - Create datasets: Author high-quality prompts, responses, and exemplars to build training and evaluation datasets, following detailed specifications and editing machine-written or human-written outputs to standard.

 - Build and apply rubrics and taxonomies: Contribute to the design of grading criteria and rubrics, then apply them consistently to produce structured, high-quality annotations across task types.

 - Annotate and correct multimodal data: Label, audit, and rectify inaccuracies across text, image, and structured data, maintaining a high standard of data integrity and accuracy.

 - Calibrate and maintain consistency: Participate in calibration exercises and inter-annotator agreement checks to align on standards, and flag ambiguous or uncovered edge cases rather than guessing, since a single misjudgment replicated at scale degrades a model.

 - Adapt to experimental work: Take on new and evolving task types as project needs shift, applying sound judgment in areas where guidelines are still being developed.

 - Report on model performance: Surface and communicate quality and performance trends in model and agent behavior, giving cross-functional partners clear, well-evidenced feedback on where models succeed, fail, and degrade.

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 1+ years of experience in AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, content moderation, research, or a related analytical role, with exposure to quality assurance, and/or preference ranking.

 - Experience applying detailed guidelines to complex and often ambiguous content, with strong contextual and sociocultural judgment, sensitivity to nuance, tone, and register, and the ability to reason well in cases where there is no single correct answer.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: a willingness to flag unclear or uncovered edge cases rather than guess, and to work productively on novel, experimental tasks whose definitions are still evolving.

 - A sharp, curious eye for inconsistencies, subtle errors, and model failure modes, including the instinct to probe models adversarially and surface where they break. Familiarity with how large language models behave, such as hallucination, sycophancy, and instruction-following gaps, is a plus.

 - Excellent command of written English and strong reading comprehension, with the ability to clearly justify your evaluations, including why an output is correct or incorrect, high-quality or low-quality, and to write clear prompts and exemplars that explain your reasoning. Bonus points if you are fluent in another language!

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to maintain consistency across high-volume and monotonous tasks.

 - Comfort working with annotation platforms and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, Markdown, XML, and YAML.

 - Strong execution in a remote environment, including good time management, comfort using new tools, and the ability to work independently in a global, asynchronous team.

 - First Assessment: If selected to move forward, you’ll receive a multiple-choice assessment by email.

title: Product Security Engineer, North Security
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!




WHY THIS ROLE

Enterprises hand Cohere their most sensitive data and put our models inside workflows they can't afford to get wrong. Securing that means working on problems the industry hasn't settled yet, what authorization means when an agent acts on a user's behalf, how to contain tools that consume untrusted input, and whether tenant boundaries hold when a model can be steered by the data it reads. The established playbooks only take you so far.

We're hiring a Senior Product Security Engineer to work these problems alongside the engineers building the products, reviewing architecture and code, threat modeling before implementation, testing what ships, and turning what you learn into defaults other teams inherit. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an advisory one.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead security reviews. Review architecture, code, and security-sensitive changes. Identify both individual vulnerabilities and the recurring design patterns behind them.

 - Secure AI-powered products. Evaluate risks such as prompt injection, unsafe tool use, identity and delegation failures, excessive agency, data exposure, tenant isolation, and sandbox escapes.

 - Threat model new capabilities. Identify trust boundaries, abuse cases, and high-impact failure modes before implementation. Translate findings into practical, prioritized mitigations.

 - Perform hands-on testing. Investigate suspected vulnerabilities, develop proofs of concept, assess exploitability and impact, and partner with engineers through remediation.

 - Build scalable guardrails. Develop secure defaults, approved patterns, reusable controls, review requirements, and automated checks that reduce recurring risks.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a design engineer to help build and maintain Waypoint, our design system, across both the Figma library and the production codebase. This is not a "designer who codes a little" or an "engineer who dabbles in Figma" role. You should be genuinely fluent on both sides, comfortable defining a component's behavior and states in Figma one hour and shipping the same component to npm the next.

You'll take direct ownership of the Figma side of our library (structure, variants, tokens, documentation) while also contributing to the core Waypoint system: our component packages, our token pipeline, and the tooling that keeps design and code in sync. If the idea of being the single point of continuity between a Figma frame and a production component sounds exciting rather than exhausting, this is your role.

We're also thinking beyond the system we have today. Waypoint isn't just meant to serve designers and engineers, it's meant to become something a model can read, reason about, and build with directly. We want someone who can help us get there: grounded enough to do the unglamorous work of making today's system solid, and forward looking enough to help define what an intelligent design system looks like next.




WHY THIS ROLE



Waypoint is still early enough that the decisions you make now will shape how the system scales. You'll have real ownership, not just a queue of component tickets, and you'll be working alongside a team that treats design and engineering as one discipline rather than two departments that hand work back and forth. And you'll be helping define what a design system becomes when it has to serve a third audience: the models that will increasingly build with it.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own and evolve the Figma library for Waypoint: component structure, variants, properties, and documentation, so it stays a reliable source of truth for design teams.

 - Build and maintain core Waypoint components, contributing directly to our component packages alongside the design engineering team.

 - Work across our token pipeline, keeping design tokens in Figma and their code representations (CSS custom properties, Tailwind config) tightly synced.

 - Partner with product designers to translate new patterns into system components, and with product engineers to make sure those components are easy to adopt correctly.

 - Help define and refine the workflows and tooling that connect Figma and code (sync scripts, plugins, documentation sites) rather than relying on manual handoff.

 - Write clear documentation and usage guidance so the system scales without you being the bottleneck.

 - Weigh in on system architecture decisions: when to add a new component versus extend an existing one, how to version and package changes, how to keep the system consistent as it grows.

 - Help shape how Waypoint evolves to serve a third consumer beyond designers and engineers: the model itself. That means thinking about how components, tokens, and patterns get structured so they're legible to AI systems, not just to humans.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Own and evolve the Figma library for Waypoint: component structure, variants, properties, and documentation, so it stays a reliable source of truth for design teams.

 - Build and maintain core Waypoint components, contributing directly to our component packages alongside the design engineering team.

 - Write clear documentation and usage guidance so the system scales without you being the bottleneck.

 - Experience building or contributing to design-to-code sync tooling (Figma plugins, token pipelines, MCP-based workflows, or similar).

 - Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG) and how to bake them into components rather than bolt them on.

 - Experience packaging and versioning component libraries for multiple consuming teams (npm scoped packages, semver, changelogs).

About the role

We are looking for a versatile corporate and regulatory lawyer to join Cohere’s Legal team. Reporting to our Senior Governance Counsel, this role will support a global portfolio of corporate governance, entity and intercompany matters, together with cross-border regulatory, trade and compliance workstreams.



This role is designed for a lawyer with a strong corporate foundation who has also developed meaningful regulatory and trade experience. You should be comfortable moving between different types of legal work including:

 - supporting global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, intercompany arrangements and delegated authorities;

 - supporting cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment and national-security reviews, regulatory diligence and filing coordination;

 - helping the business navigate export-control, sanctions and related compliance requirements; and

 - supporting legal and regulatory issues arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements come into play.
   
   

You will work closely with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams, as well as with specialist external counsel in multiple jurisdictions. The role requires sound judgment, curiosity and the ability to take ownership of a workstream, identify when specialist advice is needed, and turn that advice into practical action.



What you’ll do

 - Support Cohere’s global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, board and shareholder matters, corporate approvals, delegated authorities, signing frameworks and ongoing entity maintenance.

 - Support Cohere’s intercompany legal architecture, including intercompany agreements and other cross-border operating arrangements, working closely with Finance, Tax, People and local counsel to ensure Cohere’s entities are structured and operated appropriately across jurisdictions.

 - Support cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, regulatory diligence, filing coordination and the implementation of regulatory commitments arising in connection with acquisitions, investments, restructurings and other significant matters.

 - Support Cohere’s export-control, sanctions and related compliance matters, including coordinating specialist external advice and translating regulatory requirements into practical internal guidance, controls and documentation.

 - Support legal and regulatory workstreams arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements need to be understood and operationalised.

 - Coordinate internal stakeholders and external counsel across jurisdictions, ensuring that legal and regulatory workstreams are appropriately scoped, progressed and implemented.

 - Take ownership of matters within the role’s remit and help develop practical, scalable approaches as Cohere’s international footprint grows.

 - A qualified lawyer with approximately 4–8 years of relevant experience, gained at a leading law firm, a sophisticated in-house legal team, or preferably a combination of both.

 - A strong corporate and cross-border legal foundation, with experience across areas such as subsidiary governance, entity structuring and reorganisations, intercompany arrangements, delegated authorities, corporate approvals and other aspects of international corporate practice.

 - Meaningful exposure to cross-border regulatory matters, particularly foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, export controls, sanctions, international trade or related corporate compliance issues. Deep specialism in any one of these areas is not required.

 - Strong judgment, range and commercial awareness, with the ability to get quickly up to speed on unfamiliar issues, identify what matters most and distinguish issues that can be handled internally from those requiring specialist advice.

description:

Why this role?

Are you energized by bridging the gap between frontier AI capability and complex customer reality? Do you want to architect high-performance, resilient machine learning systems directly inside strategic enterprise environments? We are looking for a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join our team. The team is responsible for taking our large language models and making them work reliably, securely, and at peak performance within our customers' custom infrastructure and data perimeters.

In this role, you will act as the principal technical translation layer between our core engineering teams and our strategic partners. You will own the architecture for highly ambiguous, customer-specific inference challenges—ranging from multi-tenant model serving to multi-datacenter disaster recovery and custom hardware validation. You will lead technical adoption end-to-end, ensuring our models achieve exceptionally low latency, high throughput, and seamless resilience in the field.



As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will:

• Embed directly with customer engineering teams to architect the "connective tissue" between our AI models and their live, complex production environments.

• Design advanced model serving topologies, implementing multi-tenant architectures, intelligent model routing, and cross-datacenter failover strategies for multi-cluster environments.

• Optimize "AI-in-a-box" and private deployments, balancing localized SRE constraints like Kubernetes multi-cluster scale with raw model performance.

• Conduct rigorous benchmarking and profiling of customer LLM workloads, root-causing performance degradation (e.g., slow generation) via metrics, dashboards, and distributed logs.

• Accelerate hardware validation, collaborating with clients to run and support Cohere models on next-generation accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, AMD, and custom ASICs).

• Translate complex field friction into platform upgrades, delivering prescriptive feedback and contributing directly back to core product features.

• Ensure Day-1 production reliability, assisting customers in establishing sound deployment patterns, SLOs, and observability frameworks.



You may be a good fit if you have:

• 8+ years of engineering experience running production infrastructure, designing large-scale distributed systems, or deploying enterprise software in complex environments.

• Deep technical depth in production Kubernetes, including orchestration across multi-cluster and hybrid/multi-cloud ecosystems (GCP, Azure, AWS, OCI).

• Strong understanding of LLM architecture and inference dynamics, specifically how attention mechanisms, compute-bound prefill, and memory-bound decode phases dictate live performance.

• Hands-on experience with modern inference engines and optimization stacks (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, lmd, or Dynamo).

• Familiarity with distributed serving techniques, such as prefill/decode disaggregated serving, distributed KV caching, and multi-GPU workloads.

• Exceptional customer-facing technical leadership, with a proven track record of scoping highly ambiguous problems and steering executive technical stakeholders.

• The high agency, grit, and adaptability to write same-day production code while managing client-side deployment politics or blockers.

About the role:

Ray aims to provide a universal API for building distributed applications (e.g. a machine learning pipeline of feature engineering, model training, and evaluation). Data is usually a core element connecting these different stages, and therefore plays a critical role in Ray’s usability, performance, and stability. We are looking for strong engineers to build, optimize, and scale Ray’s Datasets https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/data/dataset.html library and data processing capabilities in general.



About the Ray Data team:



The Ray Data team currently develops and maintains the Ray Datasets https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/data/dataset.html library, which is already powering critical production use cases (e.g. large scale data compaction at Amazon https://www.anyscale.com/events/2022/01/20/ray-meetup-is-back-in-the-new-year-2022, and ML pipeline at Alibaba https://www.anyscale.com/blog/building-an-end-to-end-ml-pipeline-using-mars-and-xgboost-on-ray). Ray Datasets is a Python library built on top of Apache Arrow and Ray Core (Ray’s C++ backend), and the Ray Data team interacts closely with Ray Core components including the scheduler and the memory & I/O subsystems. The Ray Data team also works closely with Ray’s ML libraries including Train, RLlib, and Serve.



A snapshot of projects you will work on:

- Performance of Ray Datasets https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/data/dataset.html at large scale (leveraging Arrow primitives, optimizing Ray object manager, etc.)

- Integration with ML training and data sources

- Stability and stress testing infrastructure

- Lead future work integrating streaming workloads into Ray such as Beam on Ray

- Differentiate Data operations in Anyscale hosted Ray service





As part of this role, you will:

 - Develop high quality open source software to simplify distributed programming (Ray)

 - Identify, implement, and evaluate architectural improvements to Ray core and Datasets

 - Improve the testing process for Ray to make releases as smooth as possible

 - Communicate your work to a broader audience through talks, tutorials, and blog posts

About the role



Anyscale is looking for a Software Engineer to join the ML Developer Experience (MLDevX) team. MLDevX owns the experience layer of the Anyscale platform: the interfaces through which users and coding agents discover, configure, run, observe, debug, and productionize AI workloads. Every user journey crosses this layer through the CLI, SDKs, APIs, UI, Workspaces, MCP, or the workflows and integrations built on top of them. Together, these form the user’s primary interface into Anyscale, turning distributed computing from a systems problem back into a coding problem. We build the common contracts, tools, control-plane services, and architecture that power these surfaces.



You will work across the stack from developer tooling to cloud infrastructure and the Ray runtime. Manage long-running operations and make failures across jobs, tasks, actors, nodes, and GPUs easier to diagnose. The systems you build must scale with the platform, remain predictable through failures, and be intuitive for developers, programmable for applications, and operable by coding agents.



This is a high impact individual-contributor role with end-to-end ownership. You will work directly with users and field teams to identify high leverage problems, shape the product and technical design, and build and operate the solution. The scope spans the AI workload loop - data preparation, fine-tuning and post-training, serving, evaluation, and iteration as well as the developer loop: code, submit, monitor, debug, optimize, and re-submit. We are looking for someone with strong product judgment, a willingness to understand the user base, and the technical depth to build high quality software for everyone from a developer learning Ray for the first time to an AI-native company or enterprise running production workloads at scale.




A SNAPSHOT OF PROJECTS YOU MAY WORK ON



 - Build the next generation of developer tooling and MLOps capabilities on Ray, designed for both developers and coding agents.

 - Develop an agent-first CLI and cohesive SDK, API, and MCP surfaces with self-discovery, structured errors, dry-run support, and consistent behavior across platform resources.

 - Work across the Anyscale Workspaces stack to improve the path from local code to distributed execution, including environments, dependencies, images, authentication, workload submission, and debugging.

 - Build cohesive experience, tools and frameworks for the AI development lifecycle, including data preparation, fine-tuning and post-training, evaluation, production serving, dataset management, experiment tracking, and lineage.

 - Build the path from a trained model to a reliable production endpoint, including model registration, deployment workflows, performance benchmarking, and LLM-specific service metrics.

 - Surface observability across the CLI, SDK, UI, and agent-facing interfaces so users can diagnose failures across jobs, tasks, actors, nodes, and GPUs.

 - Design open integrations using durable standards such as OpenAI-compatible APIs and OpenTelemetry, along with stable Jobs and Services interfaces for external orchestrators.

 - Design and operate the highly available backend services and platform architecture that power these capabilities across serverless and bring-your-own-cloud environments.

 - Work closely with users and field teams to scope, ship, and iterate on the product, and collaborate with distributed systems and machine learning experts to push the boundaries of AI infrastructure.
   
   


WE'D LOVE TO HEAR FROM YOU IF YOU HAVE



 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

 - 5+ years of experience writing high-quality production code

 - A solid background in algorithms, data structures, and system design

 - Experience working with modern machine learning tooling — PyTorch, MLflow, data catalogs, and similar

 - Hands-on experience building and operating highly available services in production

 - Strong product instincts and a track record of shipping developer-facing tools that people choose to use




BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE



 - Experience building and maintaining open-source projects

 - Experience building and operating machine learning infrastructure in production

 - Experience building highly available serving systems

 - Experience using Ray

title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Systems
description:
ABOUT US:
AI NEEDS A NEW INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. WE'RE BUILDING IT AT MODAL.

Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now.


Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp https://modal.com/blog/how-ramp-built-a-full-context-background-coding-agent-on-modal, Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale.


We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation.


Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g.,Seaborn https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn,Luigi https://github.com/spotify/luigi), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience.




THE ROLE:

We’re looking for Forward Deployed Engineers on our engineering team who want to work at the intersection of deep infrastructure work and direct customer impact. As an FDE, you’ll partner with leading AI companies and foundation labs on cloud architecture, networking, storage, containerization, sandboxing, and more, helping them design and ship production infrastructure on Modal’s platform.

The FDE team today includes world-class software engineers, computational scientists, ML engineers, and former founders. We’re looking for people with strong engineering fundamentals, deep curiosity across the infrastructure stack, and energy for working directly with customers on hard problems.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON:

 - Work hands-on with companies like Suno, Lovable, Cognition, and Meta to architect and deploy massive-scale production workloads on Modal

 - Lead technical discovery and architecture sessions with prospective and existing customers

 - Architect migration paths from existing cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) to Modal’s serverless platform

 - Collaborate with Modal’s product and sales teams, contributing to the platform as both an engineer and a product stakeholder

 - Build trusted relationships with technical leaders (CTOs, VPs of Engineering, ML leads) at companies doing frontier AI work

 - Conduct technical demos, experiments, and proofs of concept that make Modal’s infrastructure advantages tangible




YOU MAY BE A FIT IF:

 - You have 3+ years of professional software engineering experience

 - You have hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), including compute, storage, networking, and container orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes)

 - You’re familiar with distributed systems architecture, data pipelines, and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation)

 - You’re a strong communicator who can go deep on systems architecture with an infrastructure team and clearly articulate tradeoffs to technical leadership

 - You have a genuine interest in working directly with customers: you find it energizing to understand someone else’s problem and help them solve it

 - You’re willing to work in person in New York City, San Francisco, or Stockholm




NICE-TO-HAVE:

 - Experience leading large-scale migration efforts, open-source contributions, or side projects you’re proud of

Cloud & Infrastructure Security

 - Improve network boundaries, service segmentation, and access controls

 - Embed security into infrastructure-as-code and deployment systems

Engineering Partnership

 - Review architecture and code for security risks and provide actionable guidance

Core Experience

What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

Linear is becoming a much broader product than people realize. With agents, mobile workflows, and new modalities, there’s a growing gap between what Linear can do and what people think it can do. This role exists to close that gap.

We’re looking for someone who will live inside the product, discover what’s possible, and show the world. That means figuring out the most compelling use cases for Linear’s AI agent, demonstrating real workflows that teams can adopt, and getting those stories out through whatever format works best, whether that’s a tweet, a video, a blog post, or a live demo at a conference. The goal is to help people understand what they can actually do with Linear and make that feel concrete and exciting.

Think of it as a product-obsessed marketer who is genuinely technical and knows how to communicate with depth.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in the US and Europe. You can work from anywhere within those regions. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you’ll do

 - Deeply understand Linear’s product, especially our AI agent and newer capabilities, and continuously discover productive, real-world use cases that teams would care about

 - Create content that demonstrates those use cases, whether that’s short-form social, blog posts, video walkthroughs, or live demos. Format follows the story, not the other way around

 - Build relationships with engineering and product-focused creators and collaborate on content that feels authentic rather than sponsored

 - Work with our video team to produce technical product content that comes across with genuine depth

 - Partner with support, sales, and product on developer-facing documentation and educational content

 - Stay plugged into the conversations happening on X, in newsletters, and at events, and make sure Linear has a voice in the ones that matter

What we’re looking for

 - Someone technical. You get code, understand how software gets built, and can talk about it credibly

 - Deep product intuition. You’re the kind of person who picks up a tool and immediately starts exploring what’s possible. You think in workflows and use cases rather than features

 - Comfortable on camera and on stage. You can demo a product, record a walkthrough, or speak at a conference without it feeling forced.

 - Twitter/X smart. You know how to use the platform, you understand what’s interesting to the people we’re trying to reach, and you can participate in the conversation with credibility

 - Curious and self-directed. You’re already finding the next interesting thing to talk about on your own, already following the right people and noticing the opportunities

WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Developer Platform https://www.notion.com/product/dev engineer, you will directly contribute to the foundational pieces that make Notion extensible and connected. You will build tools, APIs, and platform experiences that help customers connect Notion to the world — bringing their apps, data, and workflows into one workspace. Your work will make it easier for developers, admins, and builders to create reliable integrations and automations on top of Notion.


You will be a key player in building the robust technical foundation that allows Notion to achieve the connected workspace vision. Your work will include both internal platform contributions that accelerate other Notion engineering teams and end-user-facing functionality that enables toolmaking ubiquity. You will be presented with challenging technical problems, as Notion’s product needs are complex. You’ll play a key role in identifying and executing against technical investments that ensure the long-term quality, reliability, and performance of Notion’s platform as we scale.


This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - You’ll work with a team of engineers and cross-functional partners across product, design, data science, and user research to define a product strategy and drive execution through conception, research, implementation, and maintenance.

 - You’ll evolve Developer Platform capabilities across APIs, MCP tools, and integration infrastructure that help customers automate workflows, customize Notion, and connect Notion to the tools and data they use every day.

 - You’ll contribute to the overall performance, reliability, and robustness of the Notion product, ensuring it scales elegantly across many dimensions.

 - You’ll partner with engineering leaders to identify and execute against high-leverage technical investments that ensure the long-term flexibility and sustainability of our core systems.




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - 10+ years of experience shipping production software, with a strong track record of owning features end-to-end

 - Fluency with TypeScript across both backend and frontend

 - Strong product instincts: you can take a vague problem, propose a solid technical approach, and know when to cut scope

 - You don’t need to be an AI expert, but you’re curious and willing to adopt AI tools to work smarter and deliver better results




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience building developer tools like APIs and SDKs

 - Experience driving teams toward shared goals and balancing business priorities with individuals’ strengths, areas of interest, and career development goals

 - Familiarity with AI/agent tooling, evals, or LLM-driven product experiences

We’re looking for a hands-on Detection Engineer to build and operate the systems and workflows we use to detect and respond to attacks across Notion’s cloud-native environment. You’ll ship high-signal detections, improve the platform that powers them, participate in incident response, and help shape how detection and response engineering scales at Notion.




You’ll work closely with Engineering, Corporate Security, and Infrastructure, with broad latitude to identify gaps, prioritize investments, and build what’s needed next.




We view detection and response as a software engineering discipline: detections are code, platforms are products, and measurement matters




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE

 - Build and tune high-signal detections across cloud, identity, endpoint, and SaaS environments, with review and mentorship from senior teammates as you ramp up.

 - Contribute to the detection platform, including rule lifecycle management, tuning, measurement, and rollout safety.

 - Build tooling and automation that speed up triage, enrichment, investigation, and detection authoring, including LLM-based workflows where useful.

 - Turn threat intelligence and adversary TTPs into detections, telemetry requirements, and response improvements.

 - Take part in investigations, incident response, and postmortems, and help turn what we learn into lasting fixes.

 - Help define and track metrics such as coverage, MTTD, and alert quality.

 - Join a shared on-call rotation for incident response.
   




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING

 - We're hiring across a range of experience levels. If you have some of these skills but not all, we'd still like to hear from you.
   
   - 3+ years of experience in detection engineering, security operations, incident response, threat hunting, or a closely related security or software engineering role.
   
   - Have written or tuned detections that run in production, and care about signal quality and cutting noise.
   
   - Working knowledge of at least one detection or query language (Sigma, KQL, SPL, YARA-L, EQL, or Panther), or strong SQL or Python skills and the drive to learn one quickly.
   
   - An understanding of how attackers operate (for example, MITRE ATT&CK), and the ability to use it to decide what to detect.
   
   - Hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure, ideally including identity and access logs.
   
   - Have used SIEM, EDR, or SOAR tools in any size of environment.
   
   - Write clearly in runbooks, design docs, and incident notes, and can own well-scoped projects end to end.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Have led purple team, blue team, or adversary emulation exercises that improved detections or telemetry.

 - Experience applying LLMs or agent-style tooling to security workflows.

 - Generate qualified, workflow-first pipeline by identifying and targeting high-potential accounts in your assigned book, partnering with your sellers on account and outbound strategy

 - Run multi-channel outbound campaigns—email, phone, LinkedIn, and events—to create urgency and secure first meetings with the right decision-makers

 - Conduct initial qualification to ensure meetings handed to sellers are "ready to build," not just "ready to talk"—validating ICP, intent, and workflow fit before the handoff

 - Document and deliver clean handoff packets in Salesforce with ICP signals, pain points, workflow hypothesis, and stakeholder context so sellers can hit the ground running

 - Leverage GTM System tooling and intent data to sharpen targeting, prioritize accounts by signal strength, and increase the quality and consistency of your outbound motion




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - Proven track record in outbound pipeline generation, with hands-on experience in cold prospecting across phone, email, and social channels

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to craft compelling, persona-specific outreach that earns a response

 - Sharp qualification instincts—able to quickly assess ICP fit, identify urgency, and set solutions condsultants up for high-quality first conversations

 - Passion for AI/ML and understanding of API-first or consumption-based business models

 - High-activity mindset with the discipline to prioritize based on signal and data, not just volume

 - You don't need to be an AI expert, but you're curious and willing to adopt AI tools to work smarter and deliver better results.




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience with Salesforce, Outreach, or similar GTM tooling

 - Familiarity with Notion as a product or prior experience selling productivity, collaboration, or workflow software

 - Background in a high-velocity, metric-driven outbound environment with clear pipeline targets

From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Product Infrastructure team works on creating abstractions and data models that solve enduring problems across the stack. We solve problems that span multiple product surfaces and typically stretch across both front-end and backend and unblock new product avenues that were previously challenging to create.



This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - Shape and build the core frameworks that enable reading and writing data in Notion, integrating feedback from internal customers along the way, using whatever tools are required for the job, such as AWS, Postgres, NodeJS, TypeScript, React on the frontend.

 - Design new systems and abstractions that improve developer productivity, reliability, and performance by handling entire classes of problems up-front for product engineers.

 - Solve hard technical challenges such as designing abstractions for efficient traversal of the user content graph, building a system to sync user content for offline use, or scaling our permission model to serve large customers with complex content.




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - Thoughtful problem-solving: For you, problem-solving starts with a clear and accurate understanding of the context. You can decompose tricky problems and work towards a clean solution.

 - Pragmatic and business-oriented: You care about business impact and prioritize projects accordingly. You're not just going after cool stuff—you understand the balance between craft, speed, and the bottom line.

 - Strive for simplicity: You think critically about the implications of what you're building, and aim for the most simple and well-crafted design. You understand the consequence of complexity, and are motivated to eliminate them.

 - Not ideological about technology: To you, technologies and programming languages are about tradeoffs. You may be opinionated, but you're not ideological and can learn new technologies as you go.

 - Empathetic communication: You communicate nuanced ideas clearly, whether you're explaining technical decisions in writing or brainstorming in real time. In disagreements, you engage thoughtfully with other perspectives and compromise when needed.

 - Team player: For you, work isn't a solo endeavor. You enjoy collaborating cross-functionally to accomplish shared goals, and you care about learning, growing, and helping others to do the same.





NICE TO HAVES:

 - You have leveraged the features of typed languages (e.g. TypeScript, Flow) to drive code migrations, or have implemented your own data modeling paradigms (e.g. writing your own ORM, sync engine, or query language).
